To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

voltage sensor activation of the BK channel is highly cooperative with a coupling factor of ∼18 and that the voltage sensor activation increases Po mainly through increased opening rates, with little effect of voltage sensors on closing rates.

the voltage-dependent gating mechanism of BK channels is well approximated by highly constrained idealized allosterically coupled mechanisms in which voltage sensor activation increases the channel opening rate and decreases the closing rate, with little effect of voltage sensors on each other.

voltage-dependent BK channel gating can be described using a highly idealized allostersic model with coupling between the voltage-sensing and pore-gating domains, and that this coupling can be described using an allosteric cooperativity mechanism.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
voltage activation of the BK channel gating is a complex process involving multiple states, coupling between the voltage sensor and the pore gate, and cooperativity among voltage sensor states.

BK channel gating can be described by a 15-state model with five voltage sensors that can independently activate the channel, and each voltage sensor can increase the opening rate by ∼20-fold while having little or no effect on the closing rates.

the gating of BKB channels in saturating Ca+2 is well described by a highly idealized Monod-Wyamn-Changeux model in which the activation of voltage sensors increases channel opening rates while having limited effects on closing rate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
voltage sensor movement is not a simple on/off switch, but rather a complex process that increases channel activity through a complex interplay of coupling and cooperativity.
the gating of BK channels, as well as other ion channels with voltage-dependent gates, can be described by highly idealized models with only a few assumptions about the mechanisms.

the gating of BK channels can be described using simple, highly idealized allostersim, which is in stark contrast to the complex gating mechanisms that have been described for other voltage-gated ion channels.
